$comment: D-CSUBSET-PARENTHESIZED-FUNCTION-DEFINITION-DECLARATOR-REFUSED: C 6.7.6p1 permits redundant parentheses around a declarator, so `int (add)(int a, int b) { … }` defines the FUNCTION `add` — the standard glibc/musl idiom for defining a name that is also a function-like macro. MEASURED accepted-and-run by gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 18.1.3; DSS refused it three ways from one cause (the definition -> S0018 'must be a function declarator'; the parenthesized PROTOTYPE -> never recognized as a prototype, so S0002 + S0018 at the definition; the definition's own PARAMETERS -> scoped as a function pointer's, so S0001 in the body). Exercises the general form: nested parentheses, a pointer return, a prototype/definition pair, the macro idiom, and a function returning a function pointer where TWO fn-suffixes sit over ONE name (only the inner one declares it). Value-divergent: 17 + 21 + 9 - 300/60 -> exit 42. RED-ON-DISABLE: remove the parenthesis-ascent arm from `innermostNameDerivation` (semantic_analyzer.cpp) — putting the walk back to a single-level look at the name's own direct declarator — and the program no longer COMPILES (compile failure, not exit 42). The release arm re-witnesses it under the shipped pipeline.
